title: GraphScout: Empowering Large Language Models with Intrinsic Exploration Ability for Agentic Graph Reasoning

problem.claim: Graph-based retrieval methods seek to improve factual grounding and reasoning by combining LLMs with knowledge graphs.

gap.claim: Existing approaches rely on manually designed guidance and limited predefined tools, constraining graph exploration.

contributions.claim: GraphScout is a training-centric agentic graph reasoning framework with flexible graph exploration tools.
GraphScout enables autonomous knowledge-graph interaction to synthesize structured training data for post-training LLMs, reducing reliance on manual annotation and task curation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across five knowledge-graph domains, a Qwen3-4B model augmented with GraphScout reportedly outperforms baseline methods using leading LLMs by an average of 16.7% while requiring significantly fewer inference tokens.
GraphScout reportedly exhibits robust cross-domain transfer performance.
The authors report that the code is publicly available.

narrative_sequence.summary: Knowledge graphs support structured information retrieval and motivate LLM integration for factual grounding.
GraphRAG methods use iterative LLM–knowledge-graph interaction to improve reasoning.
Manual guidance and predefined tools constrain graph exploration.
GraphScout provides flexible exploration tools and uses autonomous interaction to synthesize training data for LLM post-training.
The authors report improvements across five domains, fewer inference tokens, cross-domain transfer, and public code availability.

source_observation.claim: GraphScout uses autonomous graph interaction to generate structured training data for post-training.

interpretation.claim: Internalizing exploration behavior through training may reduce dependence on manually scripted interaction guidance.

application.claim: For graph-reasoning systems, consider training models on structured interaction traces generated through flexible graph exploration.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the reported knowledge-graph domains or tasks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the baseline methods, evaluation tasks, or experimental protocols.
The abstract does not describe the graph exploration tools or training-data construction procedure in detail.
The abstract does not provide absolute performance values or token counts.
